mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 25 basis points in the past month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by more than 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% year-over-year signals strong economic growth, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 YoY growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in the past month signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to increased corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where INDPRO MoM growth exceeds 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase MoM
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL MoM growth > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs in the past month signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 jobs.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a robust economic environment, which typically boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances where UNRATE decreases and GDPC1 increases.
